title: Shatterworks: Breakable and Destruction Sound Effects
shortText: 110 breakable SFX: 10 materials, each with stress, crack, light / medium / heavy break and settle. WAV + OGG.
html:
Breakables that tell the whole story: strain, crack, break, settle

110 breakable sound effects: 10 materials, and every one ships the same 6 stages, from the strain before it gives to the debris coming to rest.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 30 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The clay pot and the glass pane complete, every stage and every take, and the medium break of the other 8 materials.

One chain, every material

A destructible prop needs more than one smash. It strains under load, it cracks (the telegraph a player can react to), it breaks softer or harder depending on the hit, and the pieces settle. Every material here ships that chain under the same names:

  • stress: the prop under load before it gives
  • crack: two takes, the first failure
  • light, medium and heavy break: two takes each
  • settle: two takes, the debris coming to rest

So you wire a breakable once and only its material changes: pot_break_heavy_02, crate_break_heavy_02, ice_break_heavy_02. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: all 10 materials carry exactly this chain, and the 150 pairs of stages inside each material all differ.

Hit it harder, it breaks bigger

A harder hit throws more pieces further, so the scatter lasts longer. For every material the three breaks are a ladder, measured on the shipped files: 20 steps, each at least 12% longer than the one below, every ladder at least 1.5x end to end. Failing steps: 0.

The materials

  • Clay pot: a fired clay pot, the breakable every dungeon is full of.
  • Porcelain vase: thin glazed porcelain: brighter than clay, with finer shards.
  • Wooden crate: a nailed plank crate: dry splinters and loose boards.
  • Barrel: staves and iron hoops: a deeper wood body with metal in the debris.
  • Glass pane: a window: a bright shatter and a long rain of shards.
  • Glass bottle: a thick bottle: a hollow pop and chunky glass.
  • Brick wall: masonry giving way: a dull crunch, rubble and dust.
  • Ice block: a block of ice: a glassy crack over a duller, wetter body.
  • Crystal: a magic crystal: its breaks run the longest of any material here.
  • Bone pile: dry bone: short, hollow knocks and a rattle as the pile collapses.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by material and stage.
  • 50 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness, so the same pot never breaks the same way twice in a row.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.97 dB, so a bone rattle and a brick wall share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1001 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised breaks designed for games, not field recordings of real objects. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No explosions, no metal (metal dents rather than breaks), no weapons and nothing musical.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Portcullis, dungeon mechanisms: the doors, chests, levers and traps around the pots you smash.
  • Steel and Bone, medieval combat impacts: the weapon hits that do the breaking.
  • Creature Vocal Forge, twelve monsters, each with idle, alert, attack, hurt, death and a special.
